    "design_critique": "1) The steering gain is cut more than the evidence supports. Effective gain per unit of normalised offset falls from kp 2.5 x weight scale 2 (= 5.0) to kp 3.0 x weight scale 0.5 (= 1.5), about 3.3 times less steering. The iteration-0 telemetry shows steering_oscillation of only 0.064 to 0.075, while max_error sat at about 0.061 and rms_error was steady at about 0.03 on all tracks. Low jitter with a steady error at the limit points to under-steering or bias on bends, not overshoot. The revision reduces steering authority, which moves the design further in the direction the data argues against. The rationale's own decision rule (raise ki or kp if max_error is near 0.06 with low oscillation) is the response this telemetry already calls for, yet the revision lowers kp in effect by 3.3 times.

2) The derivative term is not small. The rationale says an edge kick is 0.5 x 100 x 0.1 = 5 turn units. That is about four times the proportional term for the 12 mm offset (about 1.1 units at kp 3 x signal about 0.375). At 350 PWM per turn unit, 5 units is about 1750 counts. The rationale calls this 'small', which its own numbers contradict. The same concern was raised in round 1 and is not resolved. The 100/s signal-change figure is also not derived from the contract's 10 ms step, so the kick size is unverified.

3) Speed clipping is largely resolved by the speed change. At base_speed 1.5, base_pwm is 3071 with about 1024 counts of headroom, so wheel clipping starts at a turn of about 2.9. Only a full-edge reading (signal about 1) with kp 3 reaches that, so this part of the change is sound. It should be stated in the rationale, since round 1 identified clipping as the main steering loss.

4) The steering loss in iteration 0 is not diagnosed from telemetry. Progress was 0.04 to 0.115 with one line-loss event on every track, and the failure came early in each run. That pattern fits a start-up transient, a line-acquisition problem, or a sensor-lead problem, as well as high gain. Per-step data was not included, so the cause is still a hypothesis. The rationale presents it as established.

5) Speed trade-off is unquantified. The contract's objective gives 500 points for completion and about 60 x (1 - t/3) for time, so completion is worth far more than the 250 x progress term. The rationale gives up completion ('not achievable') without any estimate of achieved speed at base_speed 1.5. base_pwm 3071 (75 percent of full) with wheel lag, slip and rolling resistance may average well under 1.5 m/s. The expected progress above 0.3 is not derived. A finished run would score far above the no-completion ceiling of about 430.

6) Too many changes at once. The revision alters steering gain, base_speed, kd, ki and sensor y together. The rationale says it keeps the change 'easier to read', but five simultaneous changes make it impossible to attribute the next race result to any one of them. Round 1 asked for a cleaner test. This revision does not give one, so the decision rule cannot be applied with confidence.
